vulnerabilityAlerts.description: `enabled` is forced onto alert matches, so packages a rule sets `enabled: false` (the Expo-owned group) still get vulnerability PRs.

packageRules.description: Once a week, every non-major update lands in one PR that merges itself on green CI; one PR also means no rebasing between PRs that share pnpm-lock.yaml. Majors get a PR each, the same day, merged by hand. Security fixes skip the weekly schedule and the release age: Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts defaults open them straight away.

The weekly lock refresh from config:best-practices is how patched transitive versions arrive, so it merges itself too. Renovate cannot mix it into a group with other update types, so it stays its own PR. It has no release timestamp to age a lock refresh against, so the 3-day minimumReleaseAge above would hold it pending forever; pnpm's strict minimumReleaseAge and uv's exclude-newer enforce the age during the relock instead.

Expo owns these: the SDK pins them and Renovate cannot read bundledNativeModules.json. Matched by name only, because matchFileNames also matches the shared pnpm lockfile and a later group rule then wins. Upgrade with `just app/update` (expo install --fix + expo-doctor) at SDK upgrade time. Vulnerability alerts still raise PRs.
Stable and maintained, just slow to release. The longer threshold keeps them off the dashboard's abandoned list unless they go much quieter.

Overrides are security pins with hand-picked ranges; Renovate reads them as dependencies and proposes major bumps across the pinned range. Renovate cannot look up advisories for a range value, so `just audit` is what catches a new one. Each override names the parent package to watch; retire it once that parent moves past the vulnerable version. lightningcss is a deduplication pin, not a security pin, so Renovate keeps bumping it.

TypeScript 7.0 is the native compiler and does not expose the programmatic API that `astro check` loads, so it breaks typecheck in docs/ and www/. The TS team calls this point-in-time but has named no version; 7.1 is a probe, and docs/www typecheck in CI is the test. Widen the block if 7.1 also fails. https://github.com/withastro/roadmap/discussions/1321

Babel 8 is rejected by react-native-worklets' babel plugin, which hard-requires `^7.0.0-0`, and babel-preset-expo is still Babel 7. Every app test suite that touches a worklet fails to transform. Lift when the Expo/RN toolchain ships Babel 8 support.
Renovate rewrites this SHA-pinned rev to the tag v3.4.0, a downgrade that drops check-shebang-scripts-are-executable. Bump by hand: `prek update --freeze` keeps the SHA form.
